title: Excessive Error Disclosure - Database Constraint Error Details Exposure
description: The vulnerable error handler exposes detailed database constraint error information in HTTP responses. When a database unique constraint violation occurs (e.g., duplicate email on user creation), the vulnerable error handler catches the PostgreSQL error (code 23505) and includes the full error detail, constraint name, table name, column name, and internal query context in the HTTP response. This exposes database schema information including constraint names, table names, and column names.
impact: Database schema reconnaissance. Attackers can enumerate database schema details (table names, column names, constraint names) by triggering constraint violations. This information aids in crafting more targeted SQL injection attacks and understanding the database schema for further exploitation.
mitigation: 1) Implement secure error handler that sanitizes database errors. 2) Map database constraint errors to generic error codes (e.g., 'CONFLICT' with generic message 'Resource already exists'). 3) Log detailed database errors server-side for debugging, but return sanitized responses to clients. 4) Use secure error handler from api-secure which maps database errors to generic error codes without exposing schema details.
